articles.title: Market reactions and central bank announcements
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The market reaction to the US midterm elections was more muted than expected. US equities rose by around 1.5%, in line with gains in European and Swedish stock markets. Markets interpreted the election outcome as signalling less scope for major new fiscal spending and lower geopolitical risks. Oil prices fell to USD 94 per barrel, the US 10-year Treasury yield declined by around 5 basis points, and the dollar weakened across the board. The much-discussed rotation out of the AI sector, driven by the Democrats' tougher stance on data centres, was two-sided – falling share prices for companies directly exposed to data centre expansion, but gains for the tech giants, which are now expected to be forced to scale back investment, thereby improving cash flows.
Energy pushed euro area inflation to 4.0%.
 Core inflation remained at 2.5% and has now moved broadly sideways for several months, in line with ECB forecasts. Services inflation edged up by 0.1 percentage points, driven by base effects, but more interesting was food inflation, with prices rising for both processed and unprocessed food. Food price increases are common in October, but this could also be an early sign that higher energy prices, and perhaps drought conditions, are starting to feed through to other prices. We expect the ECB to hike rates in December, driven more by the balance of risks than by yesterday's figures.
The Bank of England is expected to hike rates to 4.00%.
 Both we and the market expect a 25bp hike. UK growth has surprised on the upside this year, while the energy shock is pushing inflation higher. We see today's hike as an insurance move rather than the start of a new tightening cycle. A follow-up hike in February is possible, but we consider market pricing of around four further hikes excessive.
Watch, listen, read:
 Today at 09:00 CET, we will broadcast Ögat Live, covering the midterm elections and the latest central bank decisions (
here
). For those who prefer listening, the latest episode of Makropodden is also available, with Jens and Elisabeth discussing the midterms (
here
). And for those who prefer reading, we continue to publish our Nordic Outlook updates, covering the US today and Sweden tomorrow.
Nordic key stories
Norges Bank is expected to stay on hold at 4.50% today.
We expect the bank to reiterate that rates need to remain elevated for some time, while keeping the door open to further hikes if the inflation outlook deteriorates. Our assessment, however, is that rates have already peaked, while markets see roughly equal probabilities of a hike and a hold in December.
The first interest rate hike in three years when the Riksbank yesterday raised it to 2.00%. 
With a more dovish press release and then a more hawkish press conference, Thedéen stressed yesterday that the increase was motivated by stronger growth and increased cost pressures, and that the increase should rather be seen as a normalisation of interest rates. We stand by our forecast of further increases in February and May, but the risk is that they will be fewer or come later. Market interest rate expectations fell slightly after the announcement, while the krona was largely unchanged against other G10 currencies.
More Swedish inflation this morning. 
We expect the CPIF to rise 0.3% at a monthly rate and that the annual rate will slow to 1.4%, while the CPIF excluding energy is expected to end at 0.4% at an annual rate, 0.2 percentage points below the Riksbank's forecast. The outcome will be a first test of yesterday's relatively fragmented view: a low figure provides arguments for a softer interpretation. In a few months' time, however, we expect rising inflation when more expensive electricity and the restored fuel tax take effect.

articles.title: Nordic Outlook Update - USA
articles.heading: Nordic Outlook (Eng)
articles.fulltext:
Our publication of Nordic Outlook in November has a slightly different format compared to other editions during the year. Under the heading Nordic Outlook Update , we are continuously publishing our forecasts and our macro view for individual countries/regions. On Tuesday 10 November, we will publish our overall view on growth, inflation, interest rates, etc., together with the table of all forecasts. 
Growth has remained resilient to shocks from trade and geopolitical conflict, and we raise our GDP forecasts again, slightly. AI investments and spending by wealthier households have made up for weaknesses elsewhere but are set to lose some momentum going forward. Slowing jobs creation and modest wage growth should keep underlying inflation contained but temporary upward pressures from energy and the AI buildout means that inflation will not be back at target until the end of 2028. The Fed raises one more time in December 2026.  
Business sentiment (ISM & PMI) has improved further after the start of the war with Iran and indicates continued solid growth. We do not expect the boom in Q3 to continue. Still, we revise our GDP forecast upwards again to 2.4 per cent in 2026, followed by 2.3 and 2.2 per cent in 2027 and 2028 respectively; 0.2 percentage points above the forecast in Nordic Outlook August for 2026 to 2027 and 0.1 for 2028. 
Fiscal policy support has limited the hit from rising gasoline prices on consumption, but the effect is fading. Sluggish employment growth, falling real earnings and weak consumer sentiment make us expect a slowdown in coming quarters. Positive wealth effects from rising equity prices are supportive but makes spending sensitive to setbacks in AI. 
Investments in data centers are expected to continue to rise at a rapid pace though higher borrowing costs could weigh on some of the plans. The AI effect on total GDP is, however, counteracted by a large import share. More generous tax depreciations rules may have contributed to a broadening into other areas. Residential construction continues to decline due to high mortgage rates. 
The labour market remains in a low hiring, no firing situation. Unemployment remains stable slightly above 4 per cent, around the Fed’s view of the longer run. Negative effects of AI have become visible in areas such as information and finance, but partly counteracted by increased employment in other sectors, such as manufacturing. 
We continue to see upward pressures on inflation from tariffs, energy prices and, to some extent, higher prices on AI-related IT, as temporary. However, a prolonged period of elevated energy prices carries risks for spreading into other prices. We have raised our forecast for core inflation slightly for 2027. Modest earnings growth, of around 3-3.5 per cent, and strong productivity growth support a return to the 2 per cent target by end 2028. 
Midterm elections and the decisive victory for Democrats in both chambers will have only limited effects on the growth outlook. Congress will be gridlocked and Democrats will get greater leverage in budget discussions. We think this may result in a slightly more expansionary fiscal policy but the door for major new spending initiatives/tax cuts is closed. A shift to Democratic governors in some states may temporarily impede the AI build-out. Fed independence will come less under pressure now after the Senate shift.

articles.title: Marknadsreaktioner och centralbanksbesked
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Marknadens reaktion över mellanårsvalet blev mildare än väntat. USA-börserna steg runt 1,5 %, i linje med uppgångarna på europeiska och svenska börser. Marknaden tolkade valresultatet som ett tecken på mindre utrymme för nya stora budgetutgifter och lägre geopolitisk risk. Oljepriset sjönk till 94 USD per fat, den amerikanska 10-årsräntan föll runt 5 punkter och dollarn tappade på bred front. Den omtalade rotationen från AI-sektorn, driven av demokraternas hårdare tag mot datacenter, var tudelad – fallande kurser för bolag direkt kopplade till utbyggnaden av datacenter, men stigande kurser för teknikjättarna som nu förväntas bli tvungna att minska sina investeringar och därmed förbättra sina kassaflöden.
Energi lyfte euroinflationen till 4,0 %.
 Kärninflationen låg kvar på 2,5 % och har nu rört sig i sidled i några månader, i linje med ECB prognoser. Tjänsteinflationen steg en tiondel drivet av baseffekter, men mer intressant var livsmedelspriserna, där både bearbetade och obearbetade varor blev dyrare. Prisuppgångar på mat är vanliga i oktober, men kan också vara ett första tecken på att energipriserna, och kanske även torkan, börjar sippra in i andra priser. Vi räknar med att ECB höjer räntan i december, mer på grund av riskbilden än gårdagens siffror.
Norges Bank väntas ligga still idag på 4,50 %.
 Vi tror att de upprepar att räntan behöver ligga högt en tid, med öppning för ytterligare höjningar om inflationsutsikterna försämras. Vår bedömning är dock att toppen redan är nådd, medan marknaden ger en höjning i december ungefär lika stor chans som en oförändrad ränta.
Bank of England väntas höja räntan till 4,00 %.
 Både vi och marknaden räknar med en höjning med 25 punkter. Brittisk tillväxt har överraskat positivt i år, samtidigt som energichocken pressar upp inflationen. Vi ser dagens höjning som en försäkringsåtgärd, inte början på en ny serie höjningar. En uppföljning i februari är möjlig, men marknadens förväntningar om omkring fyra höjningar framöver ser vi som överdrivna.
Se, lyssna, läs:
 Idag kl. 09.00 sänder vi Ögat Live om mellanårsvalet och de senaste centralbanksbeskeden (
här
). För den som gillar att lyssna finns även det senaste avsnittet av Makropodden, där Jens och Elisabeth snackar mellanårsvalet (
här
). För den som föredrar att läsa fortsätter vi att publicera våra Nordic Outlook-uppdateringar, idag USA och imorgon Sverige.
Sverige
Första räntehöjningen på tre år när Riksbanken igår höjde till 2,00 %. 
Med ett mer duvaktigt pressmeddelande och sedan en mer hökaktig presskonferens betonade Thedéen igår att höjningen motiverades av starkare tillväxt och det ökade kostnadstrycket, samt att höjningen snarare ska ses som en normalisering av räntenivån. Vi står kvar vid vår prognos om ytterligare höjningar i februari och maj, men risken är att de blir färre eller kommer senare. Marknadens ränteförväntningar sjönk något efter beskedet, medan kronan var i stort sett oförändrad mot övriga G10-valutor.
Mer svensk inflation under morgonen. 
Vi väntar oss att KPIF stiger 0,3 % i månadstakt och att årstakten dämpas till 1,4 %, medan KPIF exkl. energi väntas landa på 0,4 % i årstakt, 0,2 procentenheter under Riksbankens prognos. Utfallet blir ett första test av gårdagens relativt splittrade syn: en låg siffra ger argument för en mjukare tolkning. På några månaders sikt väntar vi oss dock stigande inflation när dyrare el och den återställda bränsleskatten slår igenom.

articles.title: Höjning – och septemberbanan står sig
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
Som väntat höjde Riksbanken styrräntan med 25 punkter till 2,00 procent den 4 november. Pressmeddelandet gav ett något duvaktigt besked om framtida höjningar, men på presskonferensen lät riksbankschef Erik Thedéen mer hökaktig. Vi håller tills vidare fast vid vår prognos om ytterligare höjningar i februari och maj, men ser risker för både färre och senare höjningar.
Mjukt besked i pressmeddelandet
Höjningen var allmänt väntad. I pressmeddelandet skrev Riksbanken att om utsikterna för inflationen och konjunkturen står sig är det troligt att styrräntan höjs ytterligare under det kommande året, i linje med räntebanan från september. Enligt vår tolkning ger beskedet inte något stöd för ännu en höjning i december och att ”styrräntan höjs under det närmaste året” antyder en risk att räntan ligger still även under första kvartalet nästa år. Att pressmeddelandet dessutom lyfte fram både uppåt- och nedåtrisker för räntan bidrar också till ett budskap åt det mjukare hållet.
Thedéen betonade tillväxt och kostnadstryck
På presskonferensen var tonläget däremot lite stramare. Thedéen återkom gång på gång till kombinationen av starkare tillväxt och högre kostnadstryck som det viktigaste skälet till höjningen. Han beskrev beslutet som en normalisering av penningpolitiken; att ”lätta på gasen” i takt med att ekonomin återhämtar sig. Thedéen lät mycket optimistisk om den svenska ekonomin och arbetsmarknaden. Samtidigt lyfte han fram hur energipriser och andra insatspriser driver på inflationen, snarare än att den underliggande inflationen har blivit något lägre än Riksbanken hade räknat med.
Om räntebanan sa Thedéen att banan från september, som pekar på upp till ytterligare två höjningar fram till september nästa år, fortfarande gäller. Han ville dock inte precisera när höjningarna kan komma.
Vi håller fast vid vår ränteprognos – tills vidare
Presskonferensen gav alltså ett lite mer hökaktigt intryck än hur vi tolkade pressmeddelandet, och det samlade budskapet låg i linje med vad vi hade väntat oss inför beslutet. Thedéen har under en tid hört till den hökaktiga delen av direktionen, och det har delvis märkts på presskonferenserna. Protokollet från mötet, som publiceras tisdagen den 10 november, blir viktigt för att bedöma när eventuella ytterligare höjningar kan komma. Tills vidare står vi fast vid vår syn att Riksbanken höjer räntan igen i februari och maj, men vi vill återigen understryka att vi ser risker för både färre och senare höjningar.
Marknadens ränteförväntningar sjönk något efter beskedet, medan kronan var i stort sett oförändrad mot de andra G10-valutorna.
Valutarisken i reserven ska minska
Riksbanken meddelade också att den kommer att minska valutariskerna i valutareserven genom att låna utländsk valuta via Riksgälden, motsvarande omkring 200 miljarder kronor. Enligt den preliminära bedömningen sker upplåningen med start 2027, förutsatt stabila marknadsförhållanden. Genomförandet skulle bestå av två delar som i dag vardera uppgår till omkring 100 miljarder kronor: dels säljer Riksbanken utländsk valuta mot kronor, dels ersätts befintliga valutaswappar, dvs avtal där två parter byter valutor med varandra under en viss tid. Hela genomförandet väntas ta 12-18 månader.
Förenklat innebär det att Riksbanken köper kronor mot utländsk valuta för omkring 100 miljarder kronor, och att Riksgälden lånar motsvarande 200 miljarder kronor i utländsk valuta. Riksgälden kommer inte att räkna in upplåningen i utländsk valuta förrän Riksbanken har fattat ett formellt beslut, och vi räknar inte med att det påverkar utgivningen av statsobligationer på något betydande sätt.
Stramare kronlikviditet i den korta änden
Kronköpen och avvecklingen av valutaswapparna gör att banksystemets likviditetsöverskott gentemot Riksbanken – de pengar bankerna sammantaget har placerade hos Riksbanken – minskar med motsvarande belopp, dvs 200 miljarder kronor. Det kommer att strama åt tillgången på kronor i den korta änden av marknaden och skulle kunna leda till ytterligare svängningar i de korta kronräntorna. Enligt Riksbanken har åtgärden inget penningpolitiskt syfte. Riksbanken kommer att lämna mer information vid decembermötet.

articles.title: Rate hike and September rate path still on track
articles.heading: Riksbank Review
articles.fulltext:
As widely expected, the Riksbank hiked the policy rate by 25bps to 2.00% but sends a slightly dovish message about future rate hikes.
The press statement said that if the outlook for inflation and economic activity holds, it is likely that the policy rate will be raised further in the coming year, in line with the policy rate forecast in September. 
To us, this does not sound like support for another near-term rate hike and given that both up- and downside risks to the rate outlook are listed in the press statement, the overall impression is on the soft side. 
However, during the press conference, Governor Thedéen kept referring to the combination of stronger growth and higher cost pressures as the key reason for the policy rate hike. He described the decision as a normalisation of the currently slightly expansionary policy rate level as the economy recovers. Thedéen sounded very optimistic on the Swedish economy and the labour market while at the same time highlighting the upward pressure on inflation from energy and other input prices, rather than the fact that underlying inflation has been somewhat lower than the Riksbank had anticipated.
On the path and the timing of hikes, Thedéen said that the September path (indicating up to two more hikes by September next year) still is valid but did not want to clarify further on the timing.
Policy conclusion:
 The press conference sounded more hawkish than we interpreted the press statement, with the overall message being much in line with what we anticipated ahead of the decision. Thedéen has belonged to the hawkish spectra of the Board for some time, and this has been partly reflected in the press conferences. The meeting minutes (published on Tuesday 10 Nov) will be important to assess the timing of potential additional rate hikes. For now, we stick with our view of further rate hikes in February and May but reiterate that we see risks of both less and delayed hikes.  
Market expectations came down somewhat following the announcement, and the SEK is roughly unchanged vs G10 peers.
Financing of the FX Reserve
The Riksbank also announced that it will reduce FX risks in the FX reserve by borrowing foreign currency via the NDO equivalent to approx. SEK 200bn.
The preliminary assessment is that, starting in 2027, and given stable market conditions, the Riksbank will borrow foreign currency via the National Debt Office equivalent to approximately SEK 200 billion. Implementation would consist, on the one hand, of the sale of foreign currency for Swedish kronor and, on the other hand, of the replacement of existing FX swaps. Each part currently amounts to around SEK 100 billion. Full implementation is expected to take 12-18 months. Simply put, this means that the Riksbank will purchase SEK vs foreign currency corresponding to about SEK100bn, while the Debt Office will borrow the equivalent of SEK200bn in FX debt. The NDO will not include the FX debt issuance until formally decided by the Riksbank, and we do not expect this to impact the SGB issuance.
The purchase of kronor and the settlement of FX swaps will result in the banking system’s liquidity surplus towards the Riksbank being reduced by a corresponding amount (i.e. 200bn). This will tighten short-end krona liquidity and could potentially cause further volatility in short SEK rate markets. Further information will be provided by the Riksbank at the December meeting. According to the Riksbank, this measure does not serve any monetary policy purpose.

articles.title: A marginal rise in existing home prices
articles.heading: Norwegian home prices
articles.fulltext:
Existing home prices rose 0.1% m/m (SA) in October, marginally below our forecast and 0.2ppt below Norges Bank’s estimate for the month. Regional differences in price developments have narrowed, although transaction times still vary considerably. The stock of homes available for sale continues to rise and is approaching its highest level since the series began. Higher mortgage rates and weak consumer confidence weigh on demand, while persistent undersupply in the new-build segment provides some support. Overall, Today’s slightly weaker figures should not materially alter Norges Bank’s broader assessment of the housing market. 
Details: 
Existing home prices fell 1.0% m/m in October, implying a 0.1% seasonal-adjusted rise. The year-on-year rate thus remains positive, albeit falling, to 1.9%, and prices so far this year have risen 3.2%. Short-term price momentum, as measured by the 3m/3m rate, slowed in early 2026 but rose somewhat in October, now at 0.4%. 
In Oslo, prices rose 0.1% m/m (SA) but were still down 0.9% YTD y/y, and the broader picture of the capital remains weak in terms of price momentum. The large sell-off of secondary homes in the capital has translated into especially weak price growth and annual growth is likely to end up below zero in 2026. However, brisk price growth since the start of the year in Trondheim and Tromsø seem to have eased, with prices declined by 0.9% m/m and 1.2% m/m in October, respectively. Nevertheless, prices in these regions still see significant YTD growth of 3.0% and 9.6%. 
Supply of existing homes approved for sales fell further in October (9.932), 5.2% lower compared to a year ago. At the same time, turnover of existing homes also declined (8.970), and were 13.4% lower compared to a year ago. The demand-supply balance thus corrected higher. Meanwhile, the stock of homes available for sale increased by 23.287, approaching its highest level since the series began. In terms of housing turnover, aggregate selling times averaged 50 days, though it varied greatly among regions. Bergen had the shortest transaction time at 19 days, whereas Fredrikstad/Sarpsborg had the highest at 90 days. 
Housing starts picked up in late 2025, but new home sales have since plummeted, delaying the recovery in developer sentiment. Although housing starts have risen modestly since before the summer, the 3m/3m rate remains at depressing levels. Combined with elevated building and material costs, this will continue to weigh on new home supply.
The 
growth in number of completed new homes 
has
 been on a steady decline since 2018
 and has dropped significantly in the past two years. A relatively stable 
situation for household formation
at the same time contributes to accumulating a structural deficit. To wit, the deficit has also shown up in the increasing rental 
prices which will absorb some of the underbuilt. 
Implications Norges Bank:
 Existing home prices rose 0.1% m/m (SA) in October, 0.2ppt below Norges Bank’s monthly projection. Large regional differences have been pulling in opposite directions, with Oslo being the weakest market this year and some west-coast region seeing the strongest price growth. These differences seem to abate which is weighing on the aggregate figures. Nevertheless, the accumulated undersupply of homes will provide a significant tailwind to price growth once mortgage rates come down. Norges Bank sees annual price growth at 3.0% in 2026, which we consider to be reasonable. Overall, though today’s figures are somewhat weaker than expected by Norges Bank, it should not alter its broader outlook of the housing market.

articles.title: No major surprises, ECB on course for another rate hike
articles.heading: Euro area inflation
articles.fulltext:
Euro area core inflation remains elevated and has moved broadly sideways over the past few months, in line with the ECB’s forecast. High energy prices push headline inflation to 4%, but today’s report offers little beyond what was generally expected. It is therefore largely a box-ticking exercise ahead of the more revealing inflation readings a few months into next year. Largely irrespective of today’s figures, elevated inflation risks will prompt the ECB to raise rates in December.
October HICP 4.0% y/y (SEB 3.8%, cons. 4.0%) and core HICP 2.5% y/y (SEB 2.4%, cons. 2.5%).
Key points
Stronger service inflation, partly due to base effects
Energy price risks are now materializing more broadly but still mostly in the HICP energy component
Slightly stronger food price increases, possibly a sign of spillover effects
The October inflation report suggests that core inflation is moving sideways in the euro area, while energy prices push headline inflation to 4%. Energy price increases are now evident across all energy components. Looking at price momentum during 2026, services prices have moved sideways, while core goods prices have strengthened. However, this upturn in core goods prices reflects developments in ICT products rather than indirect effects from energy prices. Read more 
here
. 
The September and October figures suggest softer price momentum in core goods and slightly stronger momentum in services. However, services prices have been highly volatile over the past few years, and the rise in services inflation is partly attributable to base effects.
Test of spillover effects is still ahead of us
As we have written previously, we have so far seen no signs that high energy prices have had a broader impact on inflation through indirect effects. This is also consistent with the ECB’s assessment, which various members of the Governing Council have repeatedly reiterated. The next few months will test whether, to what extent and how quickly higher energy prices feed through to core inflation.
Food and energy prices are slightly higher than expected
We see somewhat stronger increases in both food and energy prices than we expected. For food, we have seen signs of strong increases in individual economies, such as Italy, but the regional average has now also started to rise. However, there are sizeable differences across countries. Strong price momentum in October is not unusual, but it is also plausible that we are starting to see some impact from high energy prices and/or the drought earlier this year.
Energy price increases are now more broadly based, as home energy components start to rise, reflecting higher natural gas prices and their impact on electricity prices. The details suggest that home energy prices rose more than we expected, although there is considerable uncertainty about the timing and extent of the pass-through from energy prices to the relevant HICP components.
Rate hike in December despite today’s figure
We already knew that today’s figure would have a limited impact on the ECB’s assessment and was unlikely to change our expected policy trajectory. Last week’s monetary policy decision, together with comments made last week and this week, supports our view that the ECB’s next move will be a rate hike, largely irrespective of near-term inflation outcomes, read more 
here
. As we point out above, the real test for the ECB, in our view, will come early next year, when we expect indirect effects from high energy prices to feed through to other prices. The magnitude and timing of these effects will be key to the ECB’s subsequent policy moves.

articles.title: Iranian attacks in the SoH could ease with mission accomplished in US midterms
articles.heading: Crude oil comment
articles.fulltext:
A large risk premium for imminent attack on Iran has left crude oil prices.
 Brent crude fell back 1.1% yesterday. It closed at $103.6/b after having traded in a wide range of $100.8 - 107.24/b. A huge reset following the Friday closing price of $117.64/b (the Dec-26 contract). What is clear is that a large risk premium for the moment has left oil prices as Trump stood down from his threats of immediate strikes on Iran post the US midterm elections. There is still clearly a risk that Trump-Israel could choose to strike, but the sense of any immediate overhanging risk has left the market. Thus prices falling sharply. ICE Brent has traded as high as $104.96/b this morning. Following recent very high risk and prices, the appetite for piking up Brent Q1-27 at close to "only" $100/b has probably supported the buy side a little. 
But there is still a lot of risk. You cannot fully remove the risk of a new attack. We are still far from a proper resolution. It is the imminent risk of a Trump-Israel attack on Iran which has fallen back sharply.
Trump has no immediate plans of another wide attack on Iran. Probably because such an attack would be very costly.
 Trump has now stated that he has no immediate plans of striking Iran. He also commented on the fact that there haven't been any full, frontal attacks on Iran for the past six months: 
"...
if you think about it, we haven’t really had a war with them in a long time, six months, maybe more.”
. The reason for it is of course that the cost of full, frontal attacks on Iran became too high already back in April. Major energy infrastructure in the Gulf were damaged and so were a range of US military bases to the point that no US congressmen were allowed to visit them and see how bad it was. Now more than six months have passed and Iran has regrouped, rebuilt and prepared. The cost for the US and its Gulf allies (if you can call them that anymore) is now higher than at any time since April.
Iran may ease attacks in the SoH following an October peak of such attack in the runup to US midterm elections.
 Trump has already paid a dear political price for his war against Iran: The loss of both chambers in Congress. Iranian officials in October apparently stated that Iran was ramping up attacks in the SoH in the runup to the US midterm elections with the aim of impacting the elections through gasoline and diesel prices at the pump in the US. And Iranian attacks in October have been very high through October. Probably twice as high as in September. Mission accomplished. Republicans lost both chambers in the US Congress. Democrats will now have a stronger voice and it will not be so easy for Trump to get whatever money he wants for his war with Iran. This is a clear strategic win for Iran. It strengthen Iran's negotiation position. As such we could see Iran easing the attacks in the SoH back to the level in September. I.e. more oil will escape more easily from the Persian Gulf. Looking at Brent versus Oman Jan-27 futures we see Oman at $101.3/b which is well below Brent at $103.8/b. A sign that oil is indeed flowing out of the SoH. The pressure at this geographic point is easing rather than rising.
Iran and the US are indirectly negotiating in Tehran through Qatari mediators. 
But Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaee says that what the US has offered is not satisfactory. Iran want's an end to the naval blockade, a release of frozen funds and sanctions relief. It also want recognition that it together with Oman is in control of the SoH. The US wants a resolution of the nuclear issue. And there it stands.

articles.title: Hike as expected - but dovish impression
articles.heading: Riksbank comment
articles.fulltext:
Quick comment: 
Riksbank hikes by 25bps to 2%, but sends - in our view, a dovish message about future rate hikes.
Key passage:
 If the outlook for inflation and economic activity holds, it is likely that the policy rate will be raised further in the coming year, in line with the policy rate forecast in September.
To us, this does not sound like support for another near-term rate hike, and given that both up- and downside risks to the rate outlook are listed in the press statement, the overall impression is on the soft side. We await the highly interesting press conference but see downside risks to our forecast of two more rate hikes (Feb & May).
Financing of the FX Reserve
The Riksbank also announces that it will reduce FX risks in the FX reserve by borrowing foreign currency via the NDO equivalent to approx. SEK 200bn.
The preliminary assessment is that, starting in 2027, and given stable market conditions, the Riksbank will borrow foreign currency via the National Debt Office equivalent to approximately SEK 200 billion. Implementation would consist, on the one hand, of the sale of foreign currency for Swedish kronor and, on the other hand, of the replacement of existing FX swaps. Each part currently amounts to around SEK 100 billion. Full implementation is expected to take 12–18 months.
The purchase of kronor and the settlement of FX swaps will result in the banking system’s liquidity surplus towards the Riksbank being reduced by a corresponding amount (ie 200bn, if we got this right).

articles.title: Democratic sweep and Riksbank decision
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Democrats gain control of both chambers of the US Congress
, a bitter but not entirely unexpected setback for Donald Trump – who asked voters to imagine his name on the ballots. With the Democrats in control of both the House and the Senate, fiscal policy is likely to largely end up in a stalemate. While Democrats can then decide on their own economic reforms, these must also be signed by Donald Trump, who has already announced that he intends to become "Mr. Veto". At the same time, Trump retains substantial influence over foreign and trade policy, and developments in the Middle East are a key factor for both the world economy and the financial markets going forward. The White House has pushed for both escalation and renewed negotiations. Read more in Elisabet's commentary 
here.
The market has so far reacted with lower US yields, a weaker dollar and lower stock market futures, but movements are small. Asian stock market indices show a mixed performance this morning, with larger declines in Japan, and futures point to a negative opening in both Europe and the US. Democratic gains are expected to bring increased scrutiny and regulation of the AI sector, where the buildout of new data centres has been a prominent campaign issue in states such as Georgia and Texas. Democrats have been declared the winners in both states.
Yesterday:
 New headlines about progress in 
the US-Iran conflict
 caused oil and gas prices to fall rapidly yesterday and then bounce back after conflicting reports from Iranian sources. Another strong U.S. labour-market release (JOLTS) contributed to a modest rise in government bond yields. European equities generally closed slightly lower, while U.S. technology stocks found firmer footing, helping the Nasdaq finish the session up 0.8%.
Today:
 An exciting day awaits with the Riksbank rate announcement, European inflation, Norwegian home prices and the US services ISM. The market is also keeping an eye on the US Treasury's quarterly borrowing report this afternoon.
Nordic key stories
Recommended reading!
We continue to publish our Nordic Outlook updates. Denmark and Norway both see consumption rising on the back of improving household finances, but the outlook for growth and inflation diverges notably. In Norway, mainland activity is expected to stabilise in 2027-2028 after a weak first half this year, while Danish growth accelerates further on the back of very high export growth. DKK strength reduces the probability of rate hikes, while in Norway, the inflation outlook remains mixed, forcing Norges Bank to keep rates elevated until the end of next year. You can find these and all our previous updates on our 
Research page
.
The vast majority, both in our 
investor survey
 and in our 
trading room survey
, believe that the Riksbank will raise the policy rate today. 
The question is whether the Executive Board is equally unanimous or whether any of the members, Göran Hjelm and perhaps also Aino Bunge, choose to make reservations. Hjelm's previous reasoning, which emphasises the real economy consequences of the monetary policy balancing act, suggest he may see arguments for proceeding more cautiously. Swedish households carry high mortgage debt, 
and as many as 80% have floating-rate mortgages, compared with roughly 50% in 2022.
 Although consumption has finally begun to recover, households are facing strong headwinds this winter as energy prices surge. At the same time, underlying inflation is subdued and the labour market remains cool. While a rate hike today appears almost certain, there may be differing views within the Executive Board regarding the degree of tightening required. The minutes will not be published until next week, but any dissents will be announced today.
SEB's trading room survey suggests only limited market reactions
 if the Riksbank raises rates today and signals broadly unchanged risks to the policy rate path relative to September, which is also SEB's main scenario. Should the Riksbank instead signal greater upside or downside risks, market moves could be more meaningful: market rates could rise or fall by 3-6 basis points, while the Swedish krona could strengthen or weaken by around four figs, according to the average response among traders on our trading floor. The market is pricing in more than a 90 per cent probability of a hike today and a further increase of almost 90 basis points in the coming year.

articles.title: Demokratisk storseger och Riksbanksbesked
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Demokraterna tar kontroll över både representanthuset och senaten i USA
, ett surt men inte helt oväntat nederlag för Donald Trump – som bett väljarna föreställa sig att det är hans namn som står på röstsedlarna. Med Demokraterna i kontroll över båda kamrarna lär finanspolitiken i stor utsträckning hamna i ett dödläge. Visserligen kan de då besluta om egna ekonomiska reformer, men dessa måste också undertecknas av Donald Trump, som redan meddelat att han då tänker bli ”Mr Veto”. Samtidigt behåller Trump ett stort inflytande över utrikes- och handelspolitiken, och utvecklingen i Mellanöstern är en nyckelfaktor för både världsekonomin och de finansiella marknaderna framöver. Vita huset har talat om såväl eskalering som förnyade förhandlingar. Läs mer i Elisabets kommentar 
här.
Marknaden har hittills reagerat med lägre amerikanska statsräntor, en svagare dollar och fallande börsterminer, men rörelserna är små. Asiatiska börsindex visar en blandad utveckling under morgonen, med större nedgångar i Japan, och börsterminerna pekar på en negativ öppning i både Europa och USA. Demokraternas framgångar väntas leda till ökat fokus på reglering av AI-sektorn, där etableringen av nya datacenter har varit en nyckelfråga i bland annat Georgia och Texas. Demokraterna har utropats till segrare i båda dessa delstater.
Igår:
 Nya rubriker om framsteg i 
USA-Irankonflikten
 fick olje- och gaspriser att falla snabbt under gårdagen för att sedan studsa tillbaka efter motstridiga uppgifter från iranskt håll. Ytterligare en stark amerikansk jobbrapport (JOLTS) bidrog till något högre statsräntor. Europeiska börser stängde generellt svagt ned, medan amerikanska teknikaktier hittade bättre fotfäste och hjälpte Nasdaq att stänga på +0,8 procent.
Idag:
 En spännande dag väntar med Riksbanksbesked (9:30), europeisk inflation, norska bostadspriser och amerikanskt tjänste-ISM. Marknaden håller också ögonen på USA:s finansdepartements kvartalsvisa upplåningsrapport i eftermiddag.
Lästips!
 Vi fortsätter, som utlovat, att publicera våra Nordic Outlook-uppdateringar. I dag har turen kommit till våra grannar i väst, Danmark och Norge. Du hittar dessa och alla våra tidigare uppdateringar på vår 
Researchsida
.
Sverige
De allra flesta, både i vår 
investerarenkät
 och i vår 
handlarrumsenkät
, tror att Riksbanken höjer räntan i dag. 
Frågan är om direktionen är lika enig eller om någon av ledamöterna, Göran Hjelm och kanske även Aino Bunge, väljer att reservera sig. Mot bakgrund av Hjelms tidigare resonemang, som betonar de realekonomiska konsekvenserna av den penningpolitiska balansgången, finns argument för att gå mer försiktigt fram. Svenska hushåll har stora bolån och hela 80 procent har rörlig ränta, jämfört med omkring 50 procent 2022. Konsumtionen har visserligen äntligen börjat återhämta sig, men hushållen möter hård motvind i vinter när energipriserna stiger snabbt. Samtidigt är den underliggande inflationen dämpad och arbetsmarknaden fortsatt sval. Även om en räntehöjning i dag framstår som närmast kassaskåpssäker kan det finnas olika uppfattningar inom direktionen om hur mycket åtstramning som behövs. Protokollet publiceras först nästa vecka, men eventuella reservationer redovisas redan i dag.
SEB:s handlarrumsenkät tyder på mycket små marknadsreaktioner
 om Riksbanken höjer räntan i dag och signalerar ungefär oförändrade risker för ränteutsikterna jämfört med september, vilket också är SEB:s huvudscenario. Om Riksbanken i stället signalerar ökade upp- eller nedåtrisker kan reaktionerna bli större: marknadsräntor som stiger respektive faller med 3-6 baspunkter och en kronförstärkning respektive kronförsvagning på omkring 4 öre, enligt genomsnittet bland handlarna på vårt handlargolv. Marknaden prisar in mer än 90 procents sannolikhet för en höjning i dag samt ytterligare närmare 90 räntepunkters höjningar under det kommande året.

articles.title: Nordic Outlook Update - Norway
articles.heading: Nordic Outlook (Eng)
articles.fulltext:
Our publication of Nordic Outlook in November has a slightly different format compared to other editions during the year. Under the heading Nordic Outlook Update , we are continuously publishing our forecasts and our macro view for individual countries/regions. On Tuesday 10 November, we will publish our overall view on growth, inflation, interest rates, etc., together with the table of all forecasts. 
A weak first half of 2026 will weigh on mainland GDP growth this year. Activity is expected to stabilise near trend in 2027-2028, with recovering household consumption driving growth as petroleum-related demand impulses fade. The inflation outlook remains mixed. A stronger krone dampens core inflation in 2027, but high wage growth will sustain services inflation. As inflation gradually recedes, Norges Bank will deliver two rate cuts by end-2027, and one in 2028, bringing the policy rate to 3.75 per cent.
Mainland GDP growth was subdued in H1 2026, prompting a downward revision to the full-year growth forecast. Household consumption was particularly weak, as car purchases slumped in Q1 following frontloaded demand late last year ahead of changes to EV tax incentives, while Easter effects further dampened consumption in Q2. Underlying activity remains resilient, while sentiment indicators point to stable growth momentum into year-end.
The expected shift in growth drivers remains intact as petroleum-related demand impulses will turn negative from next year. Easing cost pressure and lower interest rates will gradually improve the outlook for interest-sensitive sectors, particularly residential construction and consumer durables. This will help to stabilise mainland GDP growth near trend in 2027-2028.
The 2027 budget proposal confirmed that fiscal policy will remain mildly expansionary though demand impulses will gradually fade in coming years. The minority government will face tough negotiations with support parties, but petroleum revenue spending is expected to remain at 2.7 per cent of the Government Pension Fund Global. 
Recovering household consumption, supported by real wage gains and low unemployment, will drive growth. Weak consumer confidence still encourages precautionary savings, but the consumption outlook will improve in 2027 as inflation and borrowing costs normalises.
The labour market remains stable, with modestly upbeat hiring plans and a sideway trend in job vacancies pointing to resilient labour demand. The large discrepancy between unemployment metrics will narrow. While the LFS jobless rate will edge down to 4.4 per cent in 2028, registered unemployment will increase marginally to its pre-pandemic level.
CPI-ATE inflation (CPI excl. taxes and energy) eased over the summer but remains elevated. The outlook is mixed, with high wage costs sustaining services inflation while a stronger NOK dampens imported goods prices. We see upside risks to Norges Bank’s near-term forecast, but expect a faster decline in 2027, bringing inflation closer to target in early 2028.
We project that the policy rate has peaked but risks are skewed to the upside in the near term as Norges Bank has signalled a readiness to act if the inflation outlook deteriorates materially. Gradually lower inflation paves way for policy normalisation starting in late 2027. We expect a policy rate of 3.75 per cent by end-2028, which is in the upper-end of Norges Bank’s neutral nominal rate band.

articles.title: Blue Sweep as voters turn their back on Trump
articles.heading: US elections
articles.fulltext:
Democrats have taken control over both chambers of Congress in a stunning rebuke to President Trump who asked voters to imagine he was on the ballot. Trump will be able to continue to wield power through executive orders and will likely use his veto to block Democratic legislation. Congress is now in gridlock. 
The Democratic Party is on track for a landslide victory in the US midterm elections. According to news desks, Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, after having flipped key races in North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, Ohio, Iowa and Kansas, while holding on to their seats in Georgia and New Hampshire. Democrats only needed a net gain of four Senate seats and according to AP they have now secured 52 seats, enough to overcome the casting vote of vice President Vance. Republicans have 40 seats and 8 still to be called. In the House, Democrats have reached 194 seats, with 218 needed for control and 126 yet to be called.
Gridlocked Congress could lead to slightly more expansionary fiscal policy
We expect a shift in power of Congress to lead to a slightly more expansionary fiscal policy while closing the door for major spending pushes – like President Trump’s demand for 1.5 trillion to Pentagon in the budget. This is not a bad thing for bond markets given that budget deficits are already on an unsustainable path but not enough for a sustainable improvement either. Neither party, including the president, currently seems to be focused on the budget deficit. 
Trump will be forced to negotiate
A change of power will lead to a gridlocked Congress where neither party is likely to be able to pass legislation on their own. This closes the doors for new fiscal reforms from the White House which will now have to negotiate with Democrats on budget issues and on raising the debt ceiling in 2027. We expect Democrats to use their new leverage to reverse some of the savings in health care – extending subsidies for Affordable Care Act which increased sharply this year and are expected to rise further in 2027 and work demands for Medicaid – in exchange for spending on the military. New government shutdowns are likely, but this was the case even if control of Congress had not shifted, given the need to pass annual appropriations by bipartisan support.
Mr Veto will stop Democratic legislation
With House control, Democrats will take over the Speakership and have the right to put votes on the floor. However, even if Democrats pass legislation in both chambers, they will struggle to turn them into law given the need of a signature from President Trump. A 2/3 majority in both chambers are needed to overcome a presidential veto. President Trump has already declared that he will be “Mr Veto”. 
Debt ceiling fight will give Democrats another point of leverage
Republicans have historically used the debt ceiling fights to push through spending cuts, but Democrats are not fiscal hawks and have not been as aggressive in negotiations about the debt ceiling historically. 
Investigations and impeachments
A shift in the House will also open for investigations and impeachment procedures against the President and cabinet members. A control of the Senate opens up for impeachment trials though convictions remain unlikely given the need for a super majority (2/3 of present votes). We also expect Democrats to call company CEO:s with ties to the Trump administration as witnesses. 
Trump unlikely to shift the balance in the Fed
A shift in the Senate will block the administration’s ability to appoint new members to the Fed, the Supreme Court, to the cabinet and to agencies. This means that former Fed Chair Powell can choose to retire without risking being replaced by a Trump pick. The Trump administration’s new attempts to fire Lisa Cook will not open up a new seat for them either. Having fewer members of the Board may turn the Fed more hawkish given that the Presidents of the regional Reserve Banks have tended to be more hawkish than the Board. 
President retains power over foreign, immigration and trade policy
The President retains a lot of room for maneuver within foreign, immigration and trade policy which have been in focus for his agenda and relying on executive orders rather than decisions in Congress. We do not expect a shift in control of Congress to stop the war in Iran or to stop the administration from imposing more tariffs. Instead, the courts, and ultimately the Supreme Court, will draw the line. 
Lame-duck session unlikely to result in major Republican changes
The next Congress is sworn in on 3 January 2027, and Republicans have a small window of opportunity to pass legislation until Congress closes ahead of Christmas. However, the Republican majority in the House is currently very slim and many members in both the House and the Senate are set to leave in the next Congress. Those who have lost their seats because of Trump endorsements of their opponents in the primaries are unlikely to be enthusiastic about supporting Trump. 
New headwinds for data center construction?
A key area of concern for markets has been the effects on AI. We do not expect major changes on the federal level. On state level, both parties have distanced themselves from the expansion of data centers. The Democratic candidates for governors in Georgia and Texas have called for temporary bans on server farm constructions – something that may force companies to negotiate concessions on demands from local residents when it comes to the effects on energy and water supplies. In both states, the Democrats have been called winners. 
Market reactions: Falling equity futures and weaker USD
Equity market futures are declining in both the US and Europe, while developments in Asia are mixed with a large decline in Japan. The USD has lost some ground vs the EUR while US yields are declining slightly. For markets, we continue to see the developments in the conflict in the Middle East as decisive. The White House has sent opposing messages about the next step – calling both for escalation and for new negotiations. 
Implications for 2028
The midterms will have implications for the 2028 elections when it comes to the balance of power within the Democratic power and President Trump’s control of the party. However, it is worth keeping in mind that Republican losses most likely are a result of discontent about rising prices and the war with Iran and not necessarily an endorsement of Democratic policies.

articles.title: Nordic Outlook Update - Denmark
articles.heading: Nordic Outlook (Eng)
articles.fulltext:
Our publication of Nordic Outlook in November has a slightly different format compared to other editions during the year. Under the heading Nordic Outlook Update , we are continuously publishing our forecasts and our macro view for individual countries/regions. On Tuesday 10 November, we will publish our overall view on growth, inflation, interest rates, etc., together with the table of all forecasts. 
We raise our growth forecasts once again. While net export continues to accelerate, we expect its contribution to normalise as domestic demand becomes the primary growth driver. Consumption will be supported by rising real wages, while business and residential investment are set to strengthen. Additionally, the DKK has strengthened recently, effectively reducing the risk of a rate hike. 
Since the Nordic Outlook in August, we have received Q2 GDP numbers that were higher than expected, leading us to raise our 2026 and 2027 forecasts to 4.1 per cent and 3.0 per cent, respectively, leaving 2028 unchanged at 2.5 per cent.
Net export remains the main driver of the strong GDP growth, but in our forecast, we assume some form of normalization to levels that are more aligned with what we normally see in core growth drivers, such as domestic demand. 
Consumers remain downbeat, and consumer confidence levels deteriorated further in October. However, consumers are still spending, and thus household consumption continues to be a positive driver of growth in the years ahead. We expect the savings rate of close to 13 per cent to come down somewhat due to falling unemployment. This should help to maintain consumer spending growth at current levels and support an improvement in consumer confidence going forward. 
Real wages are continuing to rise, and there are still positive effects from tax cuts shielding consumers from rising electricity prices. Monthly unemployment data indicates falling unemployment, and thus we expect wage increases to pick up. We expect this to happen gradually, from around 3 per cent today to 4.5 per cent at the end of 2028. 
After a couple of years with double-digit growth in house prices, the Danish housing market is seeing signs of cooling. Higher mortgage costs are starting to weigh on prices, particularly for apartments in Copenhagen. While increasing real wages and lower unemployment are likely to provide support, greater use of variable mortgages rates leaves households exposed to higher repayments in the coming 2-3 years. 
Investment should recover as high-capacity utilisation and stronger growth outside healthcare lift spending on machinery and equipment. Residential construction is also expected to pick up gradually from low levels, even if price increases slow down.
During the past months of elevated uncertainty in the Euro area, the Danish krone has acted as a safe haven, retreating from the extreme weakness we saw earlier in the year. While there has been minor intervention activity, it has not been enough to adjust the spread.
